transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um... I hope I'm not overreacting by being here, to be honest. But I guess what made me come in is that... well, the things that usually make me feel like myself have started feeling kind of flat lately. And heavy, if that makes sense? 

Like, I usually really enjoy my photography walks, and I do some mentoring with the local kids, and honestly, even just keeping a perfectly clean calendar at work usually gives me a little boost. But lately, I've just sort of... stopped initiating them. I just haven't had it in me. I didn't want to let it go too long without getting your advice, because I really want to make sure I'm doing everything right to stay on top of things. Is it okay that I came in just for that?
Has this low mood been present most days for at least two years?

Oh, no, no, definitely not two years. I mean, I try really hard to keep a positive attitude, you know? I'd say it's just been the last few weeks, maybe a month? I usually bounce back pretty quickly, and I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or making a big deal out of nothing. I just... I noticed it's been a little harder than usual lately, and I wanted to check in. I hope that's the right timeframe you're looking for? I'm sorry if I'm not explaining it well.
Have you ever had a similar episode of depression or low mood before this one?

Um... no, actually. I don't... I really don't think I've ever had a slump quite like this before. I mean, everyone has an off day here and there, right? But nothing that stuck around. 

I usually pride myself on being the upbeat one at the office, you know, keeping the executives organized and making sure everyone's smiling. So feeling this way is... well, it's pretty new for me. I hope that's a good sign? Like, maybe it means it's just a fluke and it'll pass quickly? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, doctor. Is that helpful?
Have you had any other episodes like this in the past?

No, um... no, I really haven't. Like I said, this is all pretty new to me. I usually manage to keep things pretty steady, you know? I'm usually the one making sure everyone else is doing okay. 

I'm sorry, I know you just asked me that, I hope I'm not repeating myself too much. I just want to be absolutely sure I'm giving you the right picture. But no, nothing like this in the past. Is that... is that what you'd expect to hear?
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Well, um... I guess that's actually sort of what made me decide to come in and talk to you. I really hate to admit it, because I don't want to sound ungrateful for the good things in my life, but... yeah, a little bit. 

Normally, I love taking these long photography walks on the weekends, and I do some mentoring with kids in my neighborhood, which is usually so rewarding. Even just... keeping my calendar perfectly color-coded at work usually gives me a little sense of satisfaction, you know? But lately, all of that just feels kind of... flat? And heavy. I've sort of stopped initiating those things. I feel terrible about the mentoring, especially. I just haven't had the energy to be the positive influence they need right now. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or selfish. I really am trying to push through it. Is it normal to feel that way when you're in a slump like this?
Have you had any previous episodes like this that lasted at least two weeks?

No, definitely not. Um, I know we just went over this a couple of times, and I really hope I'm not being frustrating by repeating myself, but... yeah, nothing like this has ever happened before. Never for two weeks, never even for a few days, really. 

I've always been so reliable, you know? My bosses count on me to be the steady one. So this whole thing is just... it's very out of character for me. I really want to be helpful and give you the right answers, but I just don't have any past history of this kind of thing to share. I hope that's okay? Like, maybe it's actually a good thing that this is the first time?
Have you had any thoughts that you would be better off dead?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. Um, I mean, I know I said I've been feeling a bit flat and heavy lately, but I would never... I don't have any thoughts like that. 

I really try to focus on the positives, you know? I have my mentoring, my photography... even if I'm struggling with them right now, I know they're important. I would never want to do anything that would let those kids down, or my coworkers. I know how much people rely on me to be there. 

I just want to get back to being my normal, helpful self. That's why I'm here, really, to figure out how to fix this little slump. So, no, nothing like that at all. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining myself clearly.
Have you had any periods before this one when you felt unusually down or depressed for at least two weeks?

No, um, I haven't. I know we kind of touched on this just a moment ago, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record, but... no. I've never had a period like this before, definitely not for two weeks. 

I've always been pretty good at bouncing back from things, you know? Like, if I have a bad day at work, I just color-code a new spreadsheet or go for a walk, and I'm fine. I've never been someone who gets stuck in a... a rut like this. I've always prided myself on being the cheerful, steady one in the office. 

So, yeah, no history of feeling down like this in the past. I hope I'm giving you the right information? I just want to make sure I'm answering everything correctly so you can help me get back on track.
Has this low mood been present nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Um, no, I wouldn't say every day. I mean, I really try to push through it, you know? It's just been... maybe off and on lately. 

I definitely still have good days where I feel perfectly fine, getting all my scheduling done and keeping the office running smoothly for the executives. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around moping all the time or letting my work slide, because I'm really not. So, no, not nearly every day for two solid weeks. Just a bit of a slump here and there. 

Does that help clarify things? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture so I'm not making it sound worse than it actually is.
Have you ever had a period in the past when you felt depressed or lost interest in things for at least two weeks?

Um, no, definitely not in the past either. I know you just asked something kind of similar, so I hope I didn't confuse you earlier—that's completely my fault if I wasn't clear! But no, I've never had a time where I just lost interest in things for weeks at a time. 

I've always been really dedicated to my hobbies and my work. I mean, the executives rely on me to keep the whole floor moving, so I don't really have the luxury of losing interest, you know? I always make sure I stay on top of everything and keep a good attitude. Even if I'm a little tired, I still show up and do my best. 

Does that answer what you're looking for? I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just really want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to figure this out.
Have you felt this low or down for most of the day on most days for at least two years?

Oh, gosh, no. Two years? Definitely not. I mean, I'm really sorry if I gave the impression that this has been going on for a long time, I really didn't mean to. 

I've always been a very positive person, you know? Keeping the executives organized and keeping morale up at the office, that's kind of my thing. I couldn't possibly do my job if I felt down for years at a time. I'm usually the one bringing in donuts on Fridays and making sure everyone's birthdays are celebrated. 

So, no, nothing like two years. Just recently, and even then, like I said, I try to keep my chin up. I hope I'm not making things too complicated by saying no to all these timeline questions? I just want to be a good patient and give you the right answers.
Have you been feeling this way continuously for at least two weeks?

Oh, um, no, not continuously. I know you asked about the two weeks just a moment ago, and I am so sorry if my first answer was confusing! I really hope I'm not frustrating you by making you repeat your questions, that's the last thing I want to do. 

But no, definitely not two weeks straight. Like I was saying, I always bounce back pretty quickly. I wouldn't let myself stay down for that long without pulling it together, especially with the executives needing me to be on my game. It's just been a day here or there, nothing continuous at all. 

Am I making sense? I really want to make sure I'm answering this exactly how you need me to.
Have you noticed any change in your sleep lately?

Um, my sleep? Well, I wouldn't say it's been a bad change, necessarily. I hope it's alright to say that—I just try to look on the bright side of things! 

There have been a few nights lately where I, um, I guess I only sleep for maybe two or three hours. I'll wake up way before dawn, but I promise it hasn't negatively affected my work or anything! Actually, instead of feeling tired, I feel completely refreshed and ready to just dive right into answering emails or updating the appointment lists for the bosses. 

It's honestly been kind of helpful for getting a head start on the day. I figure being extra productive is a good thing, right? I really hope that answers your question properly. Please let me know if I need to explain it better!
Have you ever had a period lasting several days when you felt unusually energized or abnormally high, compared with your usual self?

Abnormally high? Oh, um, I wouldn't use the word 'high,' necessarily. That sounds a bit extreme, and I really try to keep a professional, level head for the office. I hope you don't mind me saying that? 

But I do have these stretches where I feel, well, unusually upbeat. Like everything is just clicking perfectly and I'm totally on top of the world. It's actually a really great feeling for getting things done! 

But... I guess I should mention, just to be completely honest with you, since I want to be helpful... sometimes during those really upbeat stretches, if there's a tiny change, like if someone suddenly moves a meeting on the calendar... I can get a little sharp with people. It honestly surprises me when it happens, because I really pride myself on being accommodating and friendly to the staff. I always feel terrible if I snap even a little bit, because that's just not who I want to be. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're looking for.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least a week when you felt so abnormally energized or irritable that other people noticed you were not yourself?

Um, a whole week? And other people noticing? Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, I really try to keep things professional, especially at the office. I wouldn't want anyone thinking I was, you know, out of control or difficult to work with. That would be awful! 

I mean, like I said, I might get a tiny bit snappy if a schedule changes suddenly, but I always apologize right away, and I really don't think anyone would say I wasn't myself for a whole week. I always make sure to keep a smile on my face and stay helpful for the executives. 

I hope that's okay? I just really want to assure you that I keep things under control at work. Am I giving you the right kind of information?
Have you ever had a period when your mood was unusually elevated or expansive, not just irritable?

Um, well, like I mentioned before, I do get those times where I feel, um, really upbeat? Like I'm just sure everything is clicking perfectly and I'm totally on top of things. It feels like a really positive, productive mood, mostly! 

But, um, I guess to be completely open with you—because I want to make sure I'm doing this right—it can shift. Like, if I'm feeling that really elevated, expansive way, and then something tiny happens... like someone moves a meeting on the schedule without telling me... I can get, well, kind of sharp with people. 

It honestly surprises me when it happens, because I really try to be pleasant and accommodating all the time. It's just a quick flash of irritation, but it's there. Does that answer what you were asking about the elevated mood and the irritability? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it the way you need me to.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least four days when you felt much more energetic or active than usual?

Well, um, yes, I suppose I do get quite a bit more active for a few days at a time. But it's really all very productive! I wouldn't want you to think I'm just running around frantically or anything like that. 

During those stretches, I just feel so motivated to get things in order. I'll start, you know, rebuilding all the work templates for the executives, and then I might start making care plans, and I'll be emailing my relatives to check in, and reorganizing all the office files... all at once, really. It just feels like if I sit still, I'm dropping the ball, and I take my responsibilities very seriously. 

It's actually quite helpful for staying ahead at work. I hope that doesn't sound like too much? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I handle things.
Have you ever had a period when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

Um, well... yes, I suppose that does happen occasionally. But I always try to use that time constructively! I wouldn't want you to think I'm just pacing around the house or anything. 

There have been nights when I might only sleep for, oh, maybe two or three hours, and I'll wake up way before dawn. But I don't feel tired at all. I hope it doesn't sound like a bad thing? I just like to be as prepared and helpful as possible. Am I answering your question the right way?
During those more energetic periods, do you ever feel unusually confident or like you have special abilities?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I think I have, like, superpowers or anything strange like that. I really want to be clear about that, because I know how that might sound. 

But, um, I guess during those times when I'm getting so much done, I do feel... well, very capable? Like, maybe a little more confident than usual. It just seems like I'm the only one who can really straighten out all the doctors at work, and keep the family organized, and get the office running perfectly. 

I'll start to feel like the system I've put together is just... well, better than anyone else's judgment, if I'm being completely honest. I don't mean to sound arrogant at all! It's just that I care so much about doing a good job and making sure everyone is taken care of. I hope that doesn't make me sound difficult to work with? I really just want to be as helpful as I can. Does that make sense for what you were asking?
During those energetic periods, do you ever spend much more time than usual on projects or activities?

Well, um, yes, I suppose I do. Like I mentioned earlier, during those stretches, I just get so focused on getting everything perfectly in order. I'll spend hours rebuilding those work templates for the executives, and then I'll move right into making care plans, and emailing all my relatives to check in, and completely reorganizing the office files. 

It's just that I feel like if I sit still or take a break, I'm dropping the ball, you know? I take my job and my family so seriously, and I really want to make sure I'm doing everything I can for everyone. I don't want you to think I'm neglecting my normal duties or anything—I'm just trying to go above and beyond! I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right.
